security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU makes mip.STIP read-only for M-mode writes whenever ext_sstc (stimecmp) is present, without also checking that menvcfg.STCE=1. Per clarified spec, when stimecmp is implemented but STCE=0 (M-mode has not delegated timer to Sstc), STIP in mip must remain writable by M-mode software to inject timer interrupts to S-mode. Also applies to the mvip alias path: mvip.STIP must alias writable mip.STIP when STCE=0.
security_spec.summary: STIP read-only in mip must be gated on both stimecmp presence AND menvcfg.STCE=1; STCE=0 means M-mode retains write access to STIP for software timer injection

findings.finding: STIP write protection correctly gates on BOTH ext_sstc AND menvcfg.STCE=1. When STCE=0, the condition is false and MIP_STIP remains in the writable mask, allowing M-mode software to inject timer interrupts to S-mode.
alias_mask unconditionally includes MIP_STIP via bitwise OR, representing the correct default that mvip.STIP aliases mip.STIP. This is refined below at line 3870-3872 only when STCE=1.

mvip.STIP alias-clearance also correctly checks menvcfg.STCE. When STCE=0, STIP stays in alias_mask (mvip.STIP aliases writable mip.STIP). When STCE=1, STIP is removed from alias_mask so mvip.STIP is sourced from hardware timer, not from mip.
mvip_writable_mask includes MIP_STIP with the comment noting it aliases mip.STIP. The downstream rmw_mip64 STCE check at line 3744 handles the write-protection, so this static mask is correct.

Hardware timer IRQ delivery correctly depends on menvcfg.STCE=1. When STCE=0, the function returns early without raising STIP, so the hardware timer does not interfere with M-mode software setting STIP via mip.
When disabling the timer and STCE=0, STIP is correctly cleared via riscv_cpu_update_mip. This prevents stale STIP from persisting after M-mode clears STCE.

sip write path delegates to rmw_mvip64 (non-virtual) or rmw_vsip64 (virtual). The STCE check inside rmw_mvip64 (line 3870) correctly propagates, so sip.STIP reflects the proper alias behavior under both STCE=0 and STCE=1.
findings.snippet: ret = rmw_mvip64(env, csrno, ret_val, new_val, wr_mask & mask);

findings.finding: Migration state includes env.mip (line 453) and the sstc timer vmstate_sstc (line 501) which carries stimer/vstimer pointers. mip.STIP is correctly included in the migrated mip field, and the STCE-dependent write protection in rmw_mip64 applies identically post-migration.
